nodes.author: AshokaBudania
nodes.text: Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a respiratory virus that belongs to the Pneumoviridae family, similar to the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Here are some key points about HMPV:

nodes.author: AshokaBudania
nodes.text: Prevention: There is no vaccine for HMPV. Preventive measures include regular hand washing, avoiding close contact with sick individuals, and cleaning frequently touched surfaces.

nodes.author: AshokaBudania
nodes.text: Risk Groups: While anyone can contract HMPV, it poses a higher risk to children under 5, adults over 65, and those with compromised immune systems or chronic respiratory conditions like asthma or COPD.

nodes.author: AshokaBudania
nodes.text: Seasonality: HMPV is more active during the late winter and early spring, similar to the seasonal pattern of RSV and influenza

nodes.author: AshokaBudania
nodes.text: Transmission: The virus spreads through close contact with infected individuals via respiratory droplets from coughing or sneezing, and by touching contaminated surfaces followed by touching the mouth, nose, or eyes.

nodes.author: AshokaBudania
nodes.text: Symptoms: HMPV typically causes symptoms similar to those of the common cold, including cough, fever, nasal congestion, sore throat, and shortness of breath. In severe cases, it can lead to bronchitis or pneumonia, particularly in young children, older adults, and individuals
